[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

When autonomous AI agents generate application code and infrastructure, the resulting artifacts are indistinguishable from human-authored code in version control — there is no systematic record of which model version produced a given artifact, what context it was given, which Golden Path it selected, or when it ran. In a HIPAA/FedRAMP environment, this absence of provenance is a compliance gap: auditors cannot distinguish AI-generated artifacts from human-reviewed ones, and regulators increasingly require disclosure.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

The AI Audit Provenance Pattern defines a standardized mechanism for tagging every AI-generated artifact — code commits, infrastructure plans, pull requests, deployment manifests — with structured provenance metadata: the AI model version used, the context files loaded, the Golden Path declared, the timestamp of generation, and the human identity that authorized the generation. This metadata is written to the Compliance Evidence Store (PTN-GOV-AI-004) and referenced in version control, creating an unbroken audit trail from AI-generated artifact back to the governed context in which it was produced.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- Whenever an AI agent (in AI-assisted or autonomous mode) generates a code commit, infrastructure change, or deployment artifact
- When onboarding any AI tool to the enterprise development pipeline
- When a compliance audit requires disclosure of AI-generated content in regulated systems
- When a security incident requires reconstructing the context under which a system was built

page_texts.8:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- **Regulatory traceability**: Every AI-generated artifact can be traced to the model version, context, path, and authorizing human identity — satisfying emerging AI governance disclosure requirements.
- **Debugging and incident response**: When an AI-generated system behaves unexpectedly, provenance metadata enables reconstruction of the exact generation conditions.
- **Trust gradient**: AI-generated artifacts with full provenance metadata are auditable and trustworthy; artifacts without provenance are flagged as unverified.
- **Context version control**: Provenance records capture which version of the AI context files was active at generation time — enabling detection of context drift as a root cause of generation quality issues.
page_texts.10:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

The [Enterprise Golden Path Strategy](../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/enterprise-golden-path-strategy.md) requires "immutable audit provenance" as a component of the AI Governance Framework. The [Enterprise Architecture Verification Strategy](../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/enterprise-architecture-verification-strategy.md) includes "AI generation provenance metadata" as a required field in Compliance Evidence Store records. This pattern implements both requirements.

As AI development moves from AI-assisted (developer reviews everything) to autonomous (no human in the inner loop), the question "who built this?" changes from a version control lookup to a more complex question about model configuration and generation context. HIPAA-covered entities are required to maintain records of system changes — AI-generated changes are system changes.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

An AI agent generating code in a CI/CD pipeline operates with:
- A specific model version (which may change between runs)
- A set of context files (`.copilot/`, `SET_AI_CONTEXT.md`, catalog index) with specific content at a specific version
- A Golden Path declaration (which catalog entry the agent was instructed to follow)
- An authorization identity (the human or service account that triggered the generation)

None of this information is captured in a standard git commit. The committer identity is typically the service account running the pipeline, not a description of the generation context. Without explicit provenance capture, this information is irrecoverable after the fact.
page_texts.12:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Specific scenarios that require provenance:
- **Compliance audit**: "Was this change to our HIPAA system generated by an AI or a human?" — currently unanswerable without this pattern.
- **Incident investigation**: "This service is generating incorrect HIPAA audit events — when was it last generated and what model was used?" — the answer determines whether the root cause is a model issue, a context issue, or a path issue.
- **Context drift detection**: "Our AI agent's output quality degraded last month — did the context files change?" — provenance records the context version at each generation, enabling comparison.
- **Regulatory disclosure**: Emerging US and EU AI governance frameworks require disclosure of AI-generated content in regulated industries. Provenance metadata is the raw material for these disclosures.
page_texts.13:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- Provenance metadata must be captured atomically with the generated artifact — a post-hoc tagging step can be skipped or lost.
- The metadata schema must be stable and queryable — it is stored in the Compliance Evidence Store for years.
- The collection mechanism must work in both AI-assisted mode (developer triggers generation) and autonomous mode (pipeline triggers generation).
page_texts.15:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

The AI Audit Provenance Pattern defines a standardized provenance metadata record that is captured at artifact generation time and stored in three places: the Compliance Evidence Store (PTN-GOV-AI-004), the git commit message or PR description, and the deployment manifest annotation. The three-location redundancy ensures provenance survives even if one storage location is lost.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```
[AI Audit Provenance — Collection and Storage]

AI Agent Generation Event
        │
        ├── Metadata Collection (automated, at generation time)
        │   ├── model_id + model_version         (from AI tool API)
        │   ├── context_files_loaded + checksums  (from context loader)
        │   ├── golden_path_declared + version    (from context file)
        │   ├── generation_timestamp             (UTC, ISO 8601)
        │   ├── authorizing_identity             (human user or service account)
        │   └── generation_trigger               (event that initiated generation)
        │
        ├── Storage Target 1: Compliance Evidence Store (PTN-GOV-AI-004)
        │   └── Provenance record linked to build evidence records
        │
        ├── Storage Target 2: Git Commit / PR Description
        │   └── Structured YAML block in commit message
        │
        └── Storage Target 3: Deployment Manifest Annotation
            └── Kubernetes annotation: ai.gainwell.com/provenance-record-id
```

### Components

|---|---|---|
| Metadata Collection Agent | Captures provenance fields at the moment of AI generation | AI tool API, context loader |

page_texts.18:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

1. An AI agent is triggered to generate an artifact (by developer action or autonomous pipeline event).
2. The Metadata Collection Agent captures all provenance fields from the AI tool API and generation context before the artifact is written.
3. The provenance record is written to the Compliance Evidence Store (PTN-GOV-AI-004). The store returns a unique `provenance_record_id`.
4. The `provenance_record_id` and a human-readable provenance summary are embedded in the git commit message or PR description.
5. For infrastructure and deployment artifacts, the `provenance_record_id` is added as a Kubernetes/Terraform annotation.
6. The build evidence records for this run (from conformance gates, fitness functions, etc.) are linked to the provenance record by `provenance_record_id`.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

- **Developer-triggered generation (AI-assisted mode)**: The authorizing identity is the human developer's identity. The provenance record is attached to their PR.
- **Autonomous pipeline generation**: The authorizing identity is the service account, but the record includes the pipeline trigger event (e.g., "approved intent document ID: INT-2026-042") that authorized the generation run.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#phase-1-schema-and-collection-month-24]

#### Phase 1: Schema and Collection (Month 2–4)

1. Define the Provenance Record Schema (see configuration example below).
2. Implement the Metadata Collection Agent as a pipeline step that runs immediately before any AI generation step in the CI/CD pipeline.
3. Integrate with the Compliance Evidence Store (PTN-GOV-AI-004) to write provenance records.
4. Configure the pipeline to embed the `provenance_record_id` in commit messages using the standardized format.
page_texts.24:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#phase-2-manifest-annotation-and-reporting-month-56]

#### Phase 2: Manifest Annotation and Reporting (Month 5–6)

1. Implement the Deployment Manifest Annotator: add the `provenance_record_id` as an annotation on all Kubernetes Deployments and Terraform resource tags generated by AI agents.
2. Build the provenance reporting query: "Show me all AI-generated deployments to HIPAA-scoped systems in the last 12 months, with their model versions and Golden Paths declared."
3. Train the development team on interpreting provenance records and using them for incident investigation.
page_texts.25:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#phase-3-context-drift-detection-month-7]

#### Phase 3: Context Drift Detection (Month 7+)

1. Implement context file checksumming: store the SHA256 of each context file at generation time. Build a drift alert: when a context file checksum changes, alert the Platform Engineering team and flag the next generation run for additional review.
2. Build the AI Quality Correlation Dashboard: correlate generation quality metrics (conformance pass rates, fitness function failure rates) with context version changes and model version changes — enabling systematic identification of what changed when quality degraded.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#provenance-storage-location-decision-guide]

### Provenance Storage Location Decision Guide

Provenance data is written to three locations. Use this guide to understand the purpose of each:

| Location | Content | Audience | When Queried |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Git commit message** | Human-readable summary: `[AI-GENERATED]`, model name, path, authorized by | Developers reviewing PRs; Git log readers | During PR review; ad-hoc investigation via `git log` |
| **Kubernetes / Terraform annotation** | Machine-readable fields: `provenance-record-id`, `golden-path`, `generation-timestamp` | Runtime operators; configuration drift tools; incident responders | During live system inspection; when investigating a running deployment |
| **Evidence Store (full record)** | Complete provenance schema including context file checksums, artifact type list, build evidence links | Compliance team; auditors; AI quality correlation | During audit preparation; incident investigation; model rollout quality analysis |

**Principle:** Write all three locations for every AI generation event. The commit message is discoverable without tool access; the K8s annotation is discoverable at runtime; the Evidence Store is the queryable authoritative record. No single location is sufficient alone.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#example-4-ai-quality-correlation-dashboard-query]

#### Example 4: AI Quality Correlation Dashboard Query

This query identifies quality regressions correlated with context or model version changes. Run it whenever a fitness function pass rate drops by more than 5 percentage points:

```python
# Pseudocode — quality correlation dashboard query
def detect_quality_regression(window_days=30, threshold_drop=0.05):
    """
    Groups provenance records by context_version x model_version and
    correlates with fitness function pass rates in the evidence store.
    Returns any combinations with pass rate drop > threshold.
    """
    recent_records = provenance_store.query(
        timestamp_range=last_n_days(window_days)
    )

    # Group by (golden_path_version, context_catalog_version, model_version)
    groups = group_by(
        recent_records,
        keys=['context.golden_path_version',
              'context.context_files.catalog_index_version',
              'agent.model_version']
    )

    regressions = []
    for group_key, records in groups.items():
        build_ids = [r.build_evidence_links[0].build_id for r in records]
        pass_rate = evidence_store.fitness_function_pass_rate(
            build_ids=build_ids
        )
        baseline_pass_rate = evidence_store.fitness_function_pass_rate(
            build_ids=build_ids,
            baseline_window_days=90
        )
        if (baseline_pass_rate - pass_rate) > threshold_drop:
            regressions.append({
                'group': group_key,
                'current_pass_rate': pass_rate,
                'baseline_pass_rate': baseline_pass_rate,
                'drop': baseline_pass_rate - pass_rate,
                'sample_size': len(records)
            })

    return sorted(regressions, key=lambda r: r['drop'], reverse=True)

# Example output:
# [
#   {
#     'group': {
#       'golden_path_version': 'GP-001-v1.2.0',
#       'catalog_index_version': '1.6.0',   # <--- changed here
#       'model_version': 'claude-sonnet-4-6-20260201'
#     },
#     'current_pass_rate': 0.82,
#     'baseline_pass_rate': 0.94,
#     'drop': 0.12,
#     'sample_size': 47
#   }
# ]
```

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- Capture provenance metadata before the artifact is generated, not after. Post-hoc metadata collection can be skipped if the generation step fails or is interrupted.
- Store the checksum of context files at generation time — this is the primary mechanism for detecting context drift as a root cause of quality issues.
- Embed a human-readable provenance summary in the commit message so that developers reviewing PRs can immediately see that an artifact is AI-generated and which path was used — without needing to query the Evidence Store.
page_texts.33:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- **Incomplete metadata collection**: If the AI tool API does not expose model version, use an environment variable set at pipeline configuration time. Document this workaround in the provenance record.
- **Provenance for partial AI generation**: When a developer uses AI to generate part of a PR (e.g., one file), only that file's generation is AI-provenance-tagged. Mixed human/AI PRs should clearly differentiate which commits are AI-generated.
- **No linkage to conformance evidence**: Provenance records without links to the conformance gate and fitness function results are incomplete. The `build_evidence_links` field must always be populated before the provenance record is considered complete.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#compliance-requirements]

### Compliance Requirements

**HIPAA**: §164.312(b) audit controls — activity in systems that touch ePHI must be recorded. AI-generated changes to HIPAA-scoped systems are system activity events. This pattern ensures those events are recorded with sufficient detail to satisfy an audit.

**FedRAMP**: AU-3 (Content of Audit Records) requires that audit records contain sufficient information to establish what event occurred, when, where, by whom (or what), and the outcome. Provenance records satisfy all five AU-3 content requirements for AI generation events.

**EU AI Act (emerging)**: High-risk AI systems used in healthcare must maintain technical documentation including model versions and use conditions. Provenance records constitute part of this technical documentation.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#real-world-example-1]

### Real-World Example 1

**Context:** A security incident reveals that an eligibility service is incorrectly processing HIPAA data. Investigators need to know when this service was last AI-generated and what context was active.
**Implementation:** Query the Evidence Store for all provenance records for the eligibility service repository in the last 6 months. Results show: 3 AI generation events, the most recent on 2026-02-14 using GP-001 v1.1.0 (the older version that did not include the PHI audit event check). The current path version is 1.2.0 and includes this check. Root cause identified: service was not regenerated after the path version update.
**Outcome:** Root cause identified in under 15 minutes. The fix is to regenerate against GP-001 v1.2.0.
page_texts.41:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#real-world-example-2]

### Real-World Example 2

**Context:** A FedRAMP auditor asks: "How do you disclose AI-generated components in your FedRAMP-authorized system?"
**Implementation:** The provenance reporting query returns all AI-generated deployments in the FedRAMP boundary for the audit period. The report shows: model versions used, Golden Paths applied, percentage of code that is AI-generated vs human-authored, and conformance rates for AI-generated artifacts.
**Outcome:** A complete AI disclosure package is produced in under 10 minutes. The auditor accepts it as satisfying AU-3 content requirements.
page_texts.42:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#real-world-example-3]

### Real-World Example 3

**Context:** Platform Engineering detects a subtle quality regression: services generated in the past 3 weeks have a higher fitness function failure rate than historical baseline (18% vs 6%). The investigation needs to identify whether this is a model version change, a context file change, or a Golden Path change.

**Implementation:** The AI Quality Correlation Dashboard query groups provenance records by `context.golden_path_version` and `agent.model_version` and correlates with the evidence store's fitness function pass rates. The analysis reveals: the `catalog/index.yaml` context file was updated to version 1.6.0 on a date within the regression window, and it inadvertently removed a constraint that enforced the observability module requirement. Services generated against catalog v1.6.0 pass conformance gates (structural check) but fail fitness functions (the missing Prometheus dependency causes OBS-001 to fail).

**Outcome:** Root cause identified in 45 minutes. Context file corrected to v1.6.1. All services generated against v1.6.0 are queued for regeneration. The context drift detection mechanism is enhanced to alert on catalog index changes before they reach the generation pipeline.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#scenario-1-developer-reviewing-ai-generated-pr]

#### Scenario 1: Developer Reviewing AI-Generated PR

A developer reviewing a PR sees in the commit message: `[AI-GENERATED] Model: claude-sonnet-4-6, Golden Path: GP-001 v1.2.0`. They know immediately that this is AI-generated, which path was used, and can query the Evidence Store for the provenance record to see the full generation context if needed. Their review focus shifts from structural verification (handled by conformance gates) to semantic correctness.
page_texts.45:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#scenario-2-model-version-rollout-quality-check]

#### Scenario 2: Model Version Rollout Quality Check

The Platform Engineering team is rolling out a new model version. They query the Evidence Store to compare conformance gate pass rates for artifacts generated by the old vs. new model version across the same Golden Paths. If the new model version shows a lower pass rate on certain checks, this is flagged before the rollout is fully deployed.
page_texts.46:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#scenario-3-partial-ai-generation-in-a-mixed-pr]

#### Scenario 3: Partial AI Generation in a Mixed PR

A developer submits a PR where 3 files are AI-generated (the service skeleton) and 4 files are human-authored (custom business logic). The commit message format supports partial annotation: `[AI-GENERATED: src/main.py, src/config.py, k8s/deployment.yaml]`. The provenance record captures `output.artifact_types: ['application-code', 'k8s-manifest']` and specifies the exact file list. During the PR review, the reviewer sees which files were AI-generated and focuses structural review on the AI-generated files, while applying full semantic review to the human-authored business logic. The Evidence Store record accurately reflects that the deployment manifest is AI-generated (critical for FedRAMP infrastructure change tracking) while the business logic is human-authored.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#before-problem-state]

#### Before (Problem State)

- **AI disclosure**: "How much of our codebase is AI-generated?" — answered with "We don't know"; individual developer tool use is untracked
- **Review accountability**: PRs that are AI-generated are reviewed the same way as human-authored PRs; reviewers do not know to shift their focus to semantic correctness vs. structural verification
- **Incident investigation**: When a compliance issue is found, "was this AI-generated?" adds hours to root cause analysis; no audit trail connects generation events to build artifacts
- **Model version tracking**: When a new AI model is deployed, there is no mechanism to measure the before/after quality impact; regressions are discovered via downstream support tickets
- **Regulatory disclosure**: FedRAMP and EU AI Act AI disclosure requirements cannot be satisfied; the organization has no structured AI generation record

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#after-solution-state]

#### After (Solution State)

- **AI disclosure**: The Evidence Store reports 34% of commits contain AI-generated content, tagged with model version, context version, Golden Path, and authorizing identity
- **Review accountability**: Commit messages surface `[AI-GENERATED]` annotations with provenance IDs; reviewers know which files are AI-generated and adjust their review posture accordingly
- **Incident investigation**: A compliance issue is traced in 15 minutes: provenance record shows the service was generated against GP-001 v1.1.0 (missing the PHI audit event check that was added in v1.2.0)
- **Model version tracking**: The Quality Correlation Dashboard identifies a 12-point regression in fitness function pass rates correlated with a context file version change before any downstream impact occurs
- **Regulatory disclosure**: A complete AI disclosure package (model versions, Golden Paths, conformance rates, authorizing identities) is generated in under 10 minutes for any audit period

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-005-ai-audit-provenance-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** AI-generated artifacts in version control are indistinguishable from human-authored code — there is no systematic record of which model, context, or Golden Path produced a given artifact, creating compliance and incident response gaps.

**Solution:** Standardized provenance metadata (model version, context checksums, Golden Path declared, authorizing identity) is captured atomically at generation time and stored in three locations: the Compliance Evidence Store, the git commit message, and the deployment manifest annotation.

**When to Use:**
- Whenever an AI agent generates any artifact in the development pipeline
- When compliance audits require AI disclosure
- When investigating incidents involving AI-generated systems

**Key Benefits:**
- Every AI-generated artifact is traceable to its complete generation context
- Context drift is detectable as a root cause of quality degradation
- Regulatory AI disclosure requirements are satisfied with automated reporting

**Implementation Complexity:** Low

**Prerequisites:** Compliance Evidence Store operational (PTN-GOV-AI-004), AI tool API that exposes model version, context loader with checksum capture.

**Related Patterns:** PTN-GOV-AI-002, PTN-GOV-AI-004
